sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Cell-surface FLAG detected by antibody staining of non-permeabilized 293 cells transfected with N-terminal FLAG-NFAM1; surface signal confirmed. No functional (signalling or ligand-binding) assay was reported for the tagged construct.
sites.rationale: NFAM1 has a signal peptide spanning residues 1–42 (authoritative landmark); the mature N-terminus begins at residue 43 (Q). An N-terminal FLAG tag must be inserted after the signal-peptide cleavage site (after residue 42) to remain on the protein surface — placement upstream would be cleaved off with the signal peptide. The paper names no specific residue number, but with exactly one extracellular terminus the junction is uniquely determined: insert_after_residue = 42, residue_before = G (42), residue_after = Q (43). L3 confirms surface detection of the N-terminal FLAG tag, establishing this as a validated surface-display site. Full-length NFAM1 with an N-terminal FLAG tag was expressed in HEK 293 cells (pcDNA3.1 vector). Non-permeabilized cell-surface staining detected FLAG only on the N-terminal-tagged construct, confirming the tag is extracellular and the full-length protein is surface-displayed.

sources.claim: We detected cell surface expression of FLAG on cells that were transfected with the N-terminal but not the C-terminal tagged construct, while we detected intracellular FLAG in cells transfected with both constructs ( Supplemental Figures 1A, B ).

literature_notes: Three ledger lines (L1, L2, L3) all derive from the same PMC8793151 experiment. L1 and L2 describe construct design and transfection; L3 reports the result and is the probative clip. The C-terminal FLAG construct was also tested but FLAG was detected only intracellularly (not on the cell surface), consistent with the intracellular topology of the C-terminus (residues 186–270); it is recorded in other_positions. No internal extracellular-loop insertion is supported by any ledger line, so no internal sites are proposed.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal FLAG tag on full-length NFAM1 was detected intracellularly but not on the cell surface, consistent with the C-terminus residing in the cytoplasm (residues 186–270); not a surface-tag site.
